name: AI Organizational Architecture - Docker Migration
description: Migrate from ephemeral CLI agents to Docker-based organizational structure with hierarchical teams, coordinators, isolated containers, and persistent playbook-driven knowledge system. Combines short-lived agents with long-term organizational memory via ACE system.

phases.name: Infrastructure Templates & ACE Enhancement
phases.description: Create Docker templates, enhance ACE system with scope fields, and prepare migration infrastructure

sprints.name: ACE System Enhancement - Scope & Team Support
deliverables: ACE schema migration: Add scope, owner_id, team_id columns
Scope hierarchy: agent > team > org (inheritance logic)
acceptanceCriteria: PostgreSQL schema created with scope fields
Context injection supports --scope=agent|team|org
Agent inherits lessons from team + org scopes
Team isolation validated (marketing can't see engineering lessons)
95% backward compatibility with existing ACE queries
sprints.technicalNotes: Scope inheritance: Agent loads personal lessons (scope=agent, owner_id=X) + team lessons (scope=team, team_id=Y) + org lessons (scope=org). Priority: agent > team > org for conflicting lessons.

sprints.name: Docker Infrastructure Templates
acceptanceCriteria: Dockerfile builds successfully (multi-stage, <500MB image)
docker-compose creates isolated network for team
Per-agent MCP config prevents cross-agent access
Template generator creates complete team structure
Generated configs pass validation (yamllint, shellcheck)
sprints.technicalNotes: Dockerfile uses multi-stage build: Stage 1 (npm install), Stage 2 (runtime only). Network isolation via Docker networks. MCP config uses agent-specific environment variables.

sprints.name: Automatic Context Injection/Reflection
deliverables: Integration with orchestrate.sh (automatic invoke before/after agent spawn)
acceptanceCriteria: Context automatically injected before every agent spawn
Lessons automatically extracted from agent output
Agent receives /tmp/context-{agent-id}.json with relevant lessons
Post-completion reflection stores new lessons to ACE
Zero manual invoke required (fully automatic)
sprints.technicalNotes: Tag extraction uses NLP-lite: Extract nouns from task description (authentication → tags: auth, security). Lesson extraction uses regex patterns: 'Learned:', 'Best practice:', 'Anti-pattern:', etc.

phases.name: Pilot Team - Marketing Department
phases.description: Deploy Marketing team (10 agents + coordinator) in Docker containers with playbook-driven workflow

sprints.name: Marketing Team Infrastructure Deployment
acceptanceCriteria: Docker network 'marketing-team-net' created
10 agent containers running (email, social, analytics, etc.)
1 coordinator container running
Network isolation validated (agents can't reach other teams)
Health checks passing for all containers
sprints.technicalNotes: Agents: email-campaigns, social-publishing, analytics-data, crm-contacts, paid-ads, chatbot, sms-campaigns, competitive-intel, landing-pages, press-distribution. Each agent has isolated /dev/shm for tmpfs coordination.

sprints.name: Marketing Coordinator Agent Development
deliverables: Coordinator spawns ephemeral agents for tasks (via CLI in container)
Task assignment logic (route tasks to specialist agents)
Team performance monitoring (track agent confidence scores)
Budget tracking (monitor team API usage vs quota)
acceptanceCriteria: Coordinator receives task from Main Chat via Redis
Coordinator spawns appropriate specialist agent (email task → email-campaigns agent)
Agent loads team playbook (scope=team:marketing)
Agent completes task, stores lessons, exits
Coordinator reports result to Main Chat
Task completion time <5 minutes for simple tasks
sprints.technicalNotes: Coordinator uses .claude/skills/cfn-agent-spawning/spawn-agent.sh to spawn ephemeral agents inside coordinator container. Agents inherit coordinator's network namespace.

sprints.name: Playbook-Driven Workflow Validation
deliverables: Seed marketing playbook with 10 initial lessons
Validate lesson accumulation (playbook grows to 15+ lessons)
Performance benchmarks (task time, playbook load time)
acceptanceCriteria: Agent 1 executes task with 10 playbook lessons
Agent 1 stores 2 new lessons (playbook now 12)
Agent 2 executes task with 12 playbook lessons (sees Agent 1's lessons)
Agent 5 executes task with 18 playbook lessons (cumulative learning)
Playbook load time <500ms (fast context injection)
Lesson storage time <200ms (fast reflection)
sprints.technicalNotes: Seed playbook with marketing-specific lessons: 'Email subject lines <50 chars perform best', 'Social posts with images get 2x engagement', etc. Measure playbook growth rate over 5 tasks.

phases.name: Full Organizational Rollout
phases.description: Deploy all teams (Engineering, Sales, Support, Finance) + C-Suite agents

sprints.name: Engineering Team Deployment
acceptanceCriteria: Engineering team operational (15 agents + coordinator)
Coordinator routes backend/frontend/devops tasks to specialists
Team playbook isolated from Marketing team
Cross-team task execution validated (Engineering helps Marketing with API issue)
All 15 agents successfully load engineering playbook
sprints.technicalNotes: Engineering agents: backend-dev, frontend-dev, devops-engineer, kubernetes-specialist, database-architect, tester, load-tester, security-specialist, code-reviewer, api-designer, system-architect, performance-analyst, mobile-dev, data-engineer, ui-designer.

sprints.name: Sales & Support Teams Deployment
acceptanceCriteria: Sales team operational (8 agents: outbound, inbound, demo, account-mgmt, etc.)
Support team operational (10 agents: L1, L2, L3, onboarding, etc.)
Both teams have isolated playbooks
Cross-team coordination validated (Sales creates ticket → Support agent handles)
Team-specific MCP configs (Salesforce for Sales, Zendesk for Support)
sprints.technicalNotes: Sales agents: outbound-prospecting, inbound-qualifying, demo-specialist, proposal-writer, negotiator, account-manager, renewal-specialist, upsell-specialist. Support agents: L1-support, L2-support, L3-support, onboarding, training, documentation, bug-triager, escalation-manager, customer-success, retention.

sprints.name: Finance Team & C-Suite Deployment
acceptanceCriteria: Finance team operational (5 agents: accounting, FP&A, procurement, auditing, payroll)
C-Suite agents operational (CEO, CTO, COO, CFO, CISO)
C-Suite receives reports from all team coordinators
Strategic decision workflow validated (Coordinator escalates → C-Suite decides)
Organization-wide playbook accessible to all teams
sprints.technicalNotes: C-Suite agents are persistent (not ephemeral) - they provide strategic oversight. Team agents are ephemeral (spawn per task). C-Suite has higher priority access to resources.

sprints.name: Cross-Team Coordination & Escalation
deliverables: Resource sharing protocol (Engineering lends compute to Marketing)
acceptanceCriteria: Marketing Coordinator requests help from Engineering Coordinator
Engineering Coordinator assigns task to specialist agent
Result returned to Marketing Coordinator
Escalation validated: Blocker → Coordinator → COO → CEO decision
Resource sharing validated: Marketing borrows 2 agents from Engineering
Cross-team task completion time <10 minutes
sprints.technicalNotes: Cross-team communication via Redis pub/sub. Coordinators subscribe to coordinators:peer-channel. C-Suite subscribes to coordinators:to-csuite. Escalation logic: If coordinator can't resolve in 15 minutes, escalate to C-Suite.

phases.name: Optimization & Advanced Features
phases.description: Cost optimization, performance tuning, advanced playbook features, and production hardening

sprints.name: Playbook Intelligence & Curation
acceptanceCriteria: Duplicate lessons merged (same content, different wording)
Low-confidence lessons archived (<0.70 after 10 uses)
High-confidence team lessons promoted to org playbook (≥0.95, 50+ uses)
Playbook curator runs weekly, reports quality metrics
Playbook size reduced by 30% (deduplication + archival)
sprints.technicalNotes: Lesson similarity detection using TF-IDF cosine similarity (threshold 0.85). Promotion criteria: confidence ≥0.95, success_count ≥50, used by ≥3 teams. Archive criteria: confidence <0.70 after 10 trials.

sprints.name: Cost Optimization & Resource Management
deliverables: Budget alerts (notify when team >80% budget consumed)
Idle container detection (shutdown unused agents after 1 hour)
acceptanceCriteria: Team budget tracking accurate (within $5 variance)
Auto-scaling triggers at >80% resource utilization
Idle containers shut down after 1 hour (save $200/month)
Budget alerts sent to team coordinators
Cost reduced by 30% vs baseline (target: $15k → $10.5k/month)
sprints.technicalNotes: Budget tracking via API call counts (Redis counters). Auto-scaling uses Docker Swarm or Kubernetes HPA. Idle detection via last-heartbeat timestamp in Redis. Alert threshold: 80% budget, 90% budget, 100% budget.

sprints.name: Agent Performance Analytics
deliverables: Metrics: task completion time, confidence accuracy, playbook usage
acceptanceCriteria: Agent performance tracked (avg confidence, task time, success rate)
Dashboard shows top 10 / bottom 10 agents by performance
Underperforming agents flagged (coordinator receives alert)
Training recommendations generated (e.g., 'Agent needs more authentication lessons')
Performance trends visualized (improvement over 4 weeks)
sprints.technicalNotes: Performance metrics stored in PostgreSQL time-series table. Dashboard uses Grafana or custom React component. Training recommendations use NLP: identify low-confidence task tags, suggest relevant playbook lessons.

sprints.name: Production Hardening & Documentation
deliverables: Agent recovery testing (simulate container crash, validate restart)
Playbook backup & restore (daily PostgreSQL backups to S3)
Security audit (container isolation, MCP permissions, credential rotation)
acceptanceCriteria: Agent recovery <2 minutes (crash → restart → task resume)
Playbook backup daily to S3 (7-day retention)
Security audit passes (zero critical vulnerabilities)
Production deployment guide validated (dry-run on staging)
Epic completion report documents all deliverables, metrics, lessons
sprints.technicalNotes: Recovery testing: docker kill <container>, validate coordinator spawns replacement, new agent loads playbook, resumes task from Redis checkpoint. Security audit: Trivy scan for container vulnerabilities, MCP permission review, Redis ACL validation.

epicAcceptanceCriteria: All 5 teams operational (Marketing, Engineering, Sales, Support, Finance)
5 C-Suite agents operational (CEO, CTO, COO, CFO, CISO)
48+ agents across teams, all using playbook-driven workflow
ACE system supports scope hierarchy (agent > team > org)
Playbook accumulation validated (100+ lessons after 12 weeks)
Production deployment guide complete and validated

risks.description: Docker network isolation may break Redis coordination
risks.mitigation: Test Redis pub/sub across Docker networks in Phase 1

risks.description: PostgreSQL migration may cause ACE system downtime
risks.mitigation: Dual-write (SQLite + PostgreSQL) during Phase 1, cutover in Phase 2

risks.description: Coordinator overhead may reduce cost savings
risks.mitigation: Coordinator validated to handle 150 agents, 10-agent teams well within capacity

risks.description: Playbook growth may slow context injection
risks.mitigation: PostgreSQL indexes on tags, scope, confidence. Target <500ms load time.
